sdrive check exits 4 with doctor/permissions: No rule for mutating command(s): review:cold. Installed framework files are 1.0.0 while the CLI is 1.1.0-next.3; sdrive permissions:check also lists migrate, amend and reopen as unknown CLI rules.

findings.issue: sdrive check exits 4: the doctor reports no permission rule for the review:cold command. Installed framework files are 1.0.0 while the CLI is 1.1.0-next.3, so the governance gate is red before feature evidence is read. This blocks the review independently of the feature.

test-evidence.json records commit e6a5d2d but HEAD is 60c5c2e, so the evidence does not describe the tree being released. The recorded run is healthy and the code is unchanged between the two commits (60c5c2e touches only governance, report and evidence-bridge files), but the rule is commit === HEAD. The self-referential trap recurs on every re-run: evidence is committed, so a record inside a commit cannot equal that commit's own SHA. The 60c5c2e message leaves the residual mismatch visible for the reviewer rather than hand-editing the value.
The working tree is not clean: untracked .perch/ (a tool directory, not application code) makes git status --porcelain non-empty. The Commit Binding Rule requires a clean tree.

T8.2 is open and NFR-008's 500-item sync budget has no deployed measurement. The in-memory convex-test harness swings from 3.51 s (pass) to 5.01 s and 10.30 s (fail) at 3,500 rows and 14.9 s to 21.2 s at 15,000 rows on a byte-identical argument, so it neither proves nor refutes the 5 s budget. No production code change is justified before that number exists.
T7.3 and T7.4 remain open: no manual responsive/keyboard/French pass and no deployed HTTPS/HSTS and PWA confirmation. Both need a human at a browser and a live host.

NFR-009 has no accessibility evidence. No axe pass ran over the door console, register modal and custom questions, sponsor strip or wallet save control, so the WCAG 2.1 AA claim rests on unit-level screen assertions.

next 16.4.3 is in a vulnerable range (7 advisories, one moderate in production). The framework now aborts the first npm run build with SecurityFatalError and only succeeds on a retry, so a clean CI or Docker build is not reproducible. The full audit also reports 2 critical and 5 high advisories in dev-only tooling (tinypool via vitest).
Ten commit subjects use only task IDs (T1.x to T8.3) and do not name the feature, so CON-611 evidence depends on the task IDs rather than the subject line.

The Dockerfile uses npm install instead of npm ci, and .dockerignore excludes .env, .env.local and .env.*.local but not .env.production. The current .env.production values are placeholders, but a future real value would be baked into the image layer.
sdrive doctor warns that 5 adapter paths are unverified and that installed files are 1.0.0 while the CLI is 1.1.0-next.3.

baseline.detail: Clerk JWT issuer is configured in convex/auth.config.ts; helpers.getAuthenticatedUser rejects a missing identity.
Door and wallet use secureQuery/secureMutation with requireEventOrganizer; no raw query or mutation export was added to events, platform, audit, exports or registrations.
Helmet is Express-only and this project has no Express server.
doorSyncRateLimit and walletIssueRateLimit buckets are consumed before work in the door and wallet mutations; the settings, sponsor and question buckets are also wired.
Convex validators are declared on every new args block, and the new inputs are validated server-side in validators.ts.
Convex queries are typed and parameterized; the project assembles no query strings.
The new JSON-LD component is the one new dangerouslySetInnerHTML use, and it escapes <, >, & and the line separators before embedding. All other new rendering uses React escaping.
State-changing calls are Convex mutations authenticated by a Clerk token, not cookie-driven form posts.
No tracked dot-env files; .gitignore ignores them.
HSTS is a hosting-layer control and T7.4 (deployed HTTPS/HSTS and PWA confirmation) is still open.
